shanghai-brugada.l: Category I, the HIGHEST-scoring ECG finding. THIS IS A GATE: "none" makes the result non-diagnostic regardless of the total [none = No qualifying ECG finding (0); spontaneous-type1 = Spontaneous type 1 Brugada ECG pattern at nominal or high leads (3.5); fever-type1 = Fever-induced type 1 Brugada ECG pattern at nominal or high leads (3); type2-3-converts = Type 2 or 3 Brugada ECG pattern that converts with provocative drug challenge (2)]

Category II, the SINGLE HIGHEST-scoring clinical item - they do not add [none = No qualifying clinical history (0); arrest-vf-vt = Unexplained cardiac arrest, or documented ventricular fibrillation or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (3); nocturnal-agonal = Nocturnal agonal respirations (2); arrhythmic-syncope = Suspected arrhythmic syncope (2); unclear-syncope = Syncope of unclear mechanism or etiology (1); af-under-30 = Atrial flutter or fibrillation without alternative etiology, ONLY under 30 years of age (0.5)]

Category III, the SINGLE HIGHEST-scoring family item - they do not add [none = No qualifying family history (0); definite-brs-relative = First- or SECOND-degree relative with definite Brugada syndrome (2); suspicious-scd = Suspicious sudden cardiac death in a relative (fever, nocturnal, or Brugada-aggravating drugs) (1); unexplained-scd-negative-autopsy = Unexplained sudden cardiac death under 45 in a first- or second-degree relative WITH A NEGATIVE AUTOPSY (0.5)]
Category IV, a probable pathogenic mutation in a Brugada susceptibility gene. 0.5 point, deliberately de-weighted, and it cannot open the ECG gate.
Age. Required ONLY when the atrial fibrillation clinical item is selected, because that item scores only under 30 years and contributes nothing at or above it.
